title: [cuda] Split capture_end; stamp graph annotations via raw_cuda_graph
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #187749
* __->__ #187746
* #187741
* #187740

Split CUDAGraph::capture_end into capture_end_pre (ends capture, leaving the
template cudaGraph_t live for both keep_graph modes) and capture_end_post
(instantiate + destroy for keep_graph=false). capture_end() runs the two back to
back, so the existing C++ contract is unchanged for C++ callers. The split gives
a post-capture / pre-finalize window where the template is reachable via
raw_cuda_graph() regardless of keep_graph, so raw_cuda_graph() is relaxed to
require only has_graph_ (it no longer requires keep_graph=true).

This lets the kernel-annotation capture-id stamp read the template id off the
graph object (cudaGraphGetId via cuda.bindings on raw_cuda_graph()) in the
capture_end window, instead of fishing the in-flight graph out of
cudaStreamGetCaptureInfo at context entry. cudaGraphGetId stays in
Python/cuda.bindings, which resolves it at runtime -- a C++ call would require
building PyTorch against CUDA >= 13.1.

Test Plan:
```
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13.2/compat python test/test_cuda_graph_utils.py
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13.2/compat python test/test_cuda.py -k graph
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13.2/compat python test/test_cuda.py -k keep_graph
```

Authored with assistance from Claude (Anthropic AI assistant).
